## Problem

## Requirements

From an array of numbers, select a subsequence whose sum is as large as possible. Elements may be omitted, provided that no pair of neighboring array positions is omitted together.

## Preparation

- Build the two-state dynamic program, then compress it so that it uses O(1) auxiliary memory.
- Try a few arrays containing negative numbers by hand to ensure the exclusion restriction is handled correctly.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

This is a dynamic programming problem where you maintain two states per position: the best sum if you take the current element and the best sum if you skip it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

The key constraint is that you cannot skip two consecutive positions, so the skip state must be derived from the previous take state.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The final answer is the maximum of the take and skip states at the last position.

</details>

## Solution
